issues.description: The problem statement specifies a constructor SealSaloon(String) (it states the constructor takes the saloon name as a String and the UML shows +SealSaloon(String)), but both the provided template usage and the solution implement a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This mismatch means students following the problem will implement a constructor with a String parameter while the example/template code and reference solution expect a no-arg constructor. The solution also does not store or expose any saloon name field, so the constructor parameter described in the problem is missing entirely in the implementation artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement and the code consistent. Either (A) update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor (and remove the text about taking a saloon name), or (B) modify the template and solution to provide a constructor SealSaloon(String) and add a corresponding field (and getter) to store the saloon name. Ensure example usage in Main matches the chosen constructor signature.

issues.description: The problem text contains an internal inconsistency about the stock attribute: it first instructs that SealSaloon should have a final Stock stock initialized in the constructor (implying an instance final field initialized per-instance), but later explicitly states the stock attribute must be static and shared across all instances. The reference solution implements stock as a static final field initialized at declaration. This contradictory guidance (instance-final-in-constructor vs static-shared) can confuse students about whether stock should be an instance field initialized in the constructor or a static shared field.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement. If stock is meant to be shared across all saloons, explicitly state that it should be declared static final and may be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer, and remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor. If it should be an instance-level final field, update the notes that currently require it to be static and change the solution/template accordingly.
